title: When to reload
description:
The host checks the gameplay DLL's last-write time once per frame. It must reload only when the file has **changed** and the build has **finished**: the time has stayed the same for a few checks in a row. Write

```cpp
class ReloadWatcher
{
public:
    ReloadWatcher(long long loadedTime, int stablePolls);
    bool poll(long long fileTime);      // called once per frame with the file's current write time
    int generation() const;             // how many reloads have happened
    std::string copyName() const;       // the name of the copy to load for the current generation
};
```

- `loadedTime` is the write time of the DLL that is loaded right now.
- `poll` returns `true` exactly when the host should reload **now**: the file time differs from `loadedTime`, and this same time has now been seen on `stablePolls` consecutive polls (counting this one). After returning `true`, `loadedTime` becomes that time and `generation()` increases by one.
- If the time changes again while waiting, the count starts over for the new time.
- If the time goes back to `loadedTime` while waiting (the build was undone), stop waiting.
- `copyName()` is `"gameplay_<generation>.dll"`, starting at `gameplay_0.dll` before any reload.

```
ReloadWatcher w{ 100, 3 };
w.poll(100) == false     // unchanged
w.poll(150) == false     // changed, seen once
w.poll(150) == false     // twice
w.poll(150) == true      // three times: reload now, generation 1, copy gameplay_1.dll
w.poll(150) == false     // that is what is loaded now
```
hints: Remember the time you are waiting on and how many polls in a row have shown it. Any other time starts the count again at one.
